summary: Port five body lifecycle entry points beside the Rust solver module and validate repeated no-contact steps using the same integration macro and live Rust entry-point sequence.
regressions: 42 additional cases: zero/one/multiple batches, 63/64/65 bodies, spare capacity, static and partially locked masses, offset COMs, gravity on/off, velocity clamps, repeated frames/substeps
Copied fields, counters, pose padding resets, preserved velocity padding, and inactive/sentinel storage compare bitwise
Invalid layout/dimensions/parameters, non-finite outputs, modified inputs and truncated returned buffers are rejected
Handoff round trips exercise the body-specific comparator as well as original Coulomb buffers
differences: Production Rust physics and existing operation contracts/tolerances are unchanged. Gravity uses the whole-vector inverse-mass test, including its existing treatment of partially locked axes.
Cleanup uses a full-capacity launch instead of a smaller grid-stride launch; every slot has one writer and hub counter reset has one writer.

No-contact composition fuses independent per-body stages. It validates ordered stage arithmetic and repeated state, not inter-body synchronization, contact simulation, world inertia updates or production backend integration.
Pose conversion follows glamx 0.3.1 prepend_translation, including resetting explicit pose padding; no arithmetic change resolves or hides the retained zero-distance contact discrepancy.
CPU/Metal execution and Ascend source lowering remain separate; Ascend execution is unavailable.
